history.method_summary: Replaces random selection with uncertainty sampling, choosing the k pairs whose predicted reward logits are closest to zero (most ambiguous to the current model). This is a standard active-learning heuristic that should focus labeling on the decision boundary where information gain is highest.

Combines uncertainty sampling (pairs near the decision boundary) with feature-space diversity using a k-means++ style greedy selection. From a pool of the top 5k most uncertain pairs, we iteratively select k pairs that maximize a weighted sum of uncertainty and minimum cosine-distance to already-selected pairs, ensuring the labeled set covers diverse regions of feature space rather than clustering in one ambiguous area.

Implements a BADGE-inspired active learning strategy that constructs gradient embeddings by weighting each pair's feature vector by sigmoid(logit)*(1-sigmoid(logit)) — the expected gradient magnitude of cross-entropy loss, which peaks at the decision boundary. From the top-10k highest-norm gradient embedding candidates, k pairs are selected via k-means++ greedy maximization of minimum cosine distance, combining uncertainty sampling with gradient-space diversity to cover the most informative ambiguous regions.

Refines the BADGE k-means++ approach by operating on unnormalized gradient embeddings with Euclidean distance instead of normalized cosine distance, so uncertainty magnitude is naturally baked into the diversity metric rather than added as a separate term. Also increases the candidate pool from 10k to 15k to give k-means++ more coverage to choose from, following the original BADGE formulation more closely.

history.method_summary: Adapts the BADGE k-means++ approach by making the candidate pool size grow with round index (10k to 25k) and mixing 90% greedy farthest-point selection with 10% stochastic k-means++ sampling. The dynamic pool acknowledges that early rounds benefit from focusing on high-uncertainty pairs while later rounds need broader diversity coverage, and the stochastic component adds exploration to avoid getting stuck in local optima of the greedy approach.
